input_signals.name: Capital-and-Debt-Efficient Profit Expansion
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(MA(SUB(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1), MAX(DELTA(RATIO(dp, at), 1), DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating profitability is more durable when its improvement exceeds both growth in capital consumption and growth in debt burden.
input_signals.reasoning: The quality leg compares operating improvement with the more adverse of capital-consumption expansion and debt expansion, so it does not mechanically reward deleveraging alone. Requiring a high profitability level separately filters weak firms that merely shrink their balance sheets.

input_signals.name: Combined-Resource Fixed-Charge Coverage
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, SUB(act, lct)), ADD(dp, xint)), 3), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating margins predict stronger returns when the combination of current operating earnings and available net liquidity strongly covers depreciation and interest.
input_signals.reasoning: The coverage ratio pools one-period operating capacity with the existing liquidity reserve, directly measuring total resources available against fixed charges rather than intersecting two coverage sorts with a shared denominator. The separate margin requirement prevents accumulated liquidity from compensating for weak operations.

input_signals.name: Overhead-Shock Absorption Margin
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(SUB(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at), ABS(SUB(GROWTH(xsga, 1), GROWTH(sale, 1)))), 3), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating margins are more durable when the liquidity cushion is large relative to mismatches between SG&A growth and sales growth.
input_signals.reasoning: This integrates operating rigidity and financial capacity into a single stress-absorption measure instead of swapping one archived health leg for another. Firms receive a high quality score only when net liquidity is sufficient to offset the magnitude of their overhead adjustment mismatch.
